title: kb type-specialization spec: how syncBubbles handles type=repo/team/personal/profile/custom
description:
## Why
Once kb is the canonical sync engine, `syncBubbles` must encode the *type-specific* semantics that today live in three separate functions. We need a written spec before we touch code so reviewers can argue at the design level (cadence, sparse default, GC posture, push/pull boundary, hydration, manifest defaults) instead of in PR comments.

## Deliverable
`docs/ai/specs/kb-type-specialization.md` — one section per `api.KBType` (personal, profile, team, repo, custom, unknown). Each section answers:

- **Sync cadence** (current values: team/personal/profile = `TeamContextSyncInterval` 15s; repo = `SyncIntervalRead` 60s; see `sync_bubbles.go::kbSyncIntervalFor`).
- **Sparse default when no .sageox/sync.manifest is present** (today: ledger uses `ledger.ConfigureSparseCheckout` rolling murmur window; team uses `manifest.fallbackIncludes`; kb uses `manifest.fallbackIncludes`).
- **GC posture** (today: ledger + team = blue-green reclone in place; kb = soft .trash with 7-day grace). Spec must pick one or define when each applies.
- **Push semantics** (today: only ledger pushes — `pushMurmurCommits`. Spec must say whether type=repo bubbles inherit murmur push or whether the ledger keeps a separate write path).
- **Hydration policy** for LFS pointers (today: opt-in via `internal/lfs/hydrate.go` only; spec must define eager vs on-demand vs never per type).
- **Per-pull side effects** (whisper store registration, murmur relay, trigger-whisper emission, agent-work signal, codedb fingerprint check, sparse-checkout refresh).
- **Manifest defaults applied when missing** (per type — repo gets full clone, team gets sparse to docs/memory, personal gets sparse to user dir, custom = full).

## Read first
- `internal/daemon/sync_bubbles.go` (current cadence routing; per-bubble pull pipeline)
- `internal/daemon/sync.go::doPull` (ledger-specific behaviors to preserve)
- `internal/daemon/sync_team.go` (team-specific behaviors to preserve)
- `internal/manifest/fallback.go` (current single-default-set assumption)
- `internal/api/kb.go` for `KBType` enum
- The inventory doc from ox-yvc1.1 (this bead consumes it)

## Acceptance
- Spec covers all 6 KBType values (including `unknown`).
- Each section is unambiguous about what changes vs preserves vs becomes unsupported.
- Reviewed by Ryan (per CLAUDE.md "Required Reviews" — data access ergonomics + path locations).
- A small migration table at the end maps each old behavior in `sync.go::doPull` and `sync_team.go::doTeamSync` to the new type-specialized location.

## Risk if skipped
We pick a sparse default for personal/profile by accident in code review and quietly regress for users who relied on team-context's manifest behavior.

title: kb-superset inventory: behaviors in sync.go (ledger) + sync_team.go not yet in sync_bubbles.go
description:
## Why
The unification (ox-yvc1) cannot start until we know exactly which behaviors live in the ledger pull path (`internal/daemon/sync.go::doPull`) and team-context pull path (`internal/daemon/sync_team.go::doTeamSync` / `pullTeamContext`) that `internal/daemon/sync_bubbles.go::syncBubbles` does NOT yet replicate. Without an inventory we'll silently drop a behavior in migration and have to chase a regression.

## Deliverable
A new doc at `docs/ai/specs/kb-superset-inventory.md` enumerating, for each non-shared behavior, what it is, where it lives, and which kb type (if any) needs it preserved.

## Read first (don't skim)
- `internal/daemon/sync.go` (note: there is NO `sync_ledger.go`; ledger sync is `pullChanges`/`doPull` here, ~lines 1053-1280; ticker registration ~lines 620-820)
- `internal/daemon/sync_team.go` (full file, esp. `doTeamSync` and `pullTeamContext`)
- `internal/daemon/sync_bubbles.go` (full file)
- `internal/daemon/sync_managed.go` (the shared engine — anything already here is parity-safe)
- `internal/ledger/ledger.go::ConfigureSparseCheckout` (rolling murmur window — ledger-specific sparse logic)
- `internal/daemon/sync_gc.go` (blue-green GC for ledger + team-context)
- `internal/daemon/sync_gc_kb.go` (kb's softer .trash GC)

## Behaviors known to differ today (seed list — confirm and expand)
1. Ledger: refresh sparse checkout each pull via `ledger.ConfigureSparseCheckout` to keep murmur rolling window current (sync.go:1157-1161). Bubbles: applies `manifest.ComputeSparseSet` only at clone, no rolling refresh.
2. Ledger: `pushMurmurCommits` (sync.go:1306-1340) — ledger is the only managed repo the daemon pushes from (murmurs). Bubbles never push.
3. Ledger: `triggerLedgerIndexRebuild` + `LedgerCheckInterval` ticker — content-fingerprint-driven codedb rebuild (sync.go:1360+). Bubbles do not feed codedb.
4. Ledger: ledger mutex (`s.ledgerMu`) coordinates with GitHub sync push. Bubbles use no per-bubble mutex; rely on ls-remote dedup.
5. Ledger: dedicated agent-work signal channel after successful pull (`agentWorker.Notify`).
6. Team: anti-entropy `triggerMissingClones` for missing workspaces (sync_team.go:30).
7. Team: per-team whisper-store registration + per-pull murmur relay (sync_team.go:213-231, 287-289).
8. Team: trigger-whisper emission on detected file changes for the *primary* team only (sync_team.go:241-259) — only-primary policy is non-trivial.
9. Team: corrupt-repo move-aside backup file naming + clone-in-flight backoff via `ShouldRetryClone`.
10. Team: `applySparseCheckout` ALWAYS reapplies post-pull (sync_team.go:197-205) so manifest sparse changes propagate. Bubbles only apply at clone.
11. Team: per-workspace `SyncIntervalMin` and `GCIntervalDays` written back to registry from manifest (sync_team.go:199-205). Bubbles read manifest but do not feed registry.
12. Team: dual-counter telemetry — `RecordTeamSync` / `RecordTeamSyncError` distinct from kb's heartbeat-tagging.
13. Ledger pull: `ProgressWriter` IPC for blocking foreground `ox sync` invocations (sync.go callers via `doPull`). Bubbles loop has no progress surface.
14. Ledger: `EnsureCheckoutGitignore` runs on every pull cycle from sync_gc.go context, plus from clone path. Confirm bubbles do this on pull (sync_bubbles.go only does at clone).
15. GC: ledger reopens whisper store after blue-green swap (sync_gc.go:143-145) — needed because old `sql.DB` handle points at deleted inode.
16. GC: kb GC uses soft-delete `.trash/` with 7-day grace (sync_gc_kb.go); ledger/team GC does in-place blue-green reclone. Different semantics that need a unified policy.
17. Per-pull behavior: ledger has no `sync.manifest` on disk (manifest defaults inlined in code); team-context reads manifest each pull; kb reads manifest each pull. Confirm.
18. Sparse-set fallback: `manifest.fallbackIncludes` is biased toward team-context (`SOUL.md`, `coworkers/`, `discussions/`). Ledger uses different paths via `ConfigureSparseCheckout`. Document the per-type expected default set.

## Acceptance
- Doc exists, is reviewed by Ryan.
- Every numbered item above is either (a) confirmed-and-detailed with a code reference, (b) confirmed-not-applicable with rationale, or (c) replaced/expanded.
- Doc names each kb type that inherits each behavior (repo / team / personal / profile / custom / unknown).

## Risk if skipped
Migration beads will rediscover gaps mid-PR and ship with regressions. The 5-bug parity sweep that just closed (ox-lf6g) was caused by exactly this kind of skipped inventory.

title: [epic] KB as canonical sync engine: fold ledger + team-context as types under kb
description:
User architectural directive: "ledger and team context git repos should be a SUBSET of what kb provides!" + "kb are hyper optimized and learning from the best of team context and ledgers."

## Today's state

Three parallel sync implementations:
- internal/daemon/sync_ledger.go (ledger sync — full clone, ResolveRules, manifest)
- internal/daemon/sync_team.go (team-context sync — TwoPhaseClone, sparse, manifest)
- internal/daemon/sync_bubbles.go (kb sync — now at parity with team-context after ox-lf6g.1-.4)

KB now matches team-context feature-for-feature, but ledger and team-context still have their own loops.

## End state

One canonical sync engine: the kb sync path is the only sync path. Ledger becomes type=repo bubbles. Team contexts become type=team bubbles. Both routed through syncBubbles → pullManagedRepo. Two implementations deleted, replaced by kb specializations.

## Why now (priority)

- Eliminates a class of drift bugs (parity work just fixed 5 gaps that existed because kb was a sibling, not a superset).
- KB type-specific cadence already routes correctly (15s for personal/profile/team, 60s for repo).
- Heartbeat already tags by kb_type so observability stays whole.
- Doctor already understands kb checks; status surfaces kb summary; prime emits kb array.

The refactor's main risk is the migration window: existing ledger/team-context paths must keep working until users on older clients have migrated. Need a versioned cutover.

## Children to file
1. Inventory: list every behavior in sync_ledger.go and sync_team.go that isn't yet in sync_bubbles.go.
2. Type-specialization spec: define how syncBubbles handles type=repo (ledger semantics) vs type=team (team-context semantics) vs type=personal/profile/custom.
3. Migrate sync_ledger.go callers to syncBubbles with type=repo wiring; keep sync_ledger.go as a thin shim for one release.
4. Migrate sync_team.go callers to syncBubbles with type=team wiring; same shim approach.
5. Delete sync_ledger.go and sync_team.go after the deprecation window.
6. Update CHANGELOG, docs/ai, doctor checks to reflect the unification.

title: [epic] KB sync parity: two-phase clone, manifest, LFS, gitignore
description:
Audit of /Users/ryan/conductor/workspaces/ox/luxembourg-v6/internal/daemon/sync_bubbles.go found that kb clone path bypasses the same machinery team-context and ledger use:

| Feature | Team-ctx | KB | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two-phase clone (shallow + filter) | yes | NO | First clone 10-50× slower for large repos |
| sync.manifest parsing | yes | NO | Sparse patterns ignored; full tree always |

title: internal/kb/merge.go - three-source merger
description:
Create `internal/kb/merge.go` — the unified three-source merger used by `ox kb list`, `ox status`, prime, and the daemon sync loop.

## Behavior
Fan out IN PARALLEL to:
1. `GET /api/v1/kb` (via `internal/api/kb.go` `ListBubbles`) — new bubbles. 403 / empty / 404 are non-fatal.
2. `GET /api/v1/cli/repos` — legacy team contexts → synthesize `type=team (legacy)`.
3. Local ledger registry / project state → synthesize `type=repo (legacy)`.

## Dedup
Stable identifier merge order: `kb_id` wins; otherwise match by `repo_id`; otherwise by `slug+endpoint`. When a row exists in source #1 AND a corresponding legacy row exists in source #2 or #3, the kb-API row wins and the legacy row is suppressed.

## Failure isolation
Each source is independent. Failure of one returns a non-fatal warning attached to the result struct (something like `Result{ Bubbles []Bubble; SourceWarnings []SourceWarning }`). Caller decides how to render warnings. NEVER fail the whole list because one source errored.

## Escape hatch
Honor `OX_KB_DISABLE=1` env var — when set, skip source #1 entirely (legacy-only mode). Mirrors the `OX_XDG_DISABLE` pattern.

## Reference
- `internal/api/kb.go` (F1) — KB source
- `internal/api/ledger.go` and the team-contexts client in `cmd/ox/init.go` — legacy sources
- Plan section "Should `ox kb list` include legacy team contexts + ledgers?" for the design rationale.
close_reason: three-source merger with parallel fan-out, dedup, and OX_KB_DISABLE escape hatch

title: internal/api/kb.go - KB API client
description:
Create the KB HTTP API client at `internal/api/kb.go`, mirroring the style of `internal/api/ledger.go`.

## Methods
- `ListBubbles(ctx context.Context) ([]Bubble, error)` → `GET /api/v1/kb`
- `GetBubble(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Bubble, error)` → `GET /api/v1/kb/{id}`

## Response handling
- 200: parse JSON list / object
- 404 / 403: return non-fatal sentinel error (e.g. `ErrKBSourceUnavailable`). The KB API is one of three always-queried sources — failure here must NOT fail the whole listing in `internal/kb/merge.go`.
- 5xx / network errors: standard wrapped error

## Types
Define a `Bubble` struct with at least: `KBID`, `Type` (personal|profile|team|repo|custom|unknown), `Slug`, `Name`, `LifecycleState`, `ViewerRole`, `RepoURL`, plus whatever the server returns. Use `type=unknown` as the client-side fallback bucket for forward compatibility.

## Caching
Per-CLI-invocation 5-min TTL cache for `ListBubbles` so we don't pay for repeat calls within a short window. Daemon caches per-lifetime (handled by daemon, not the client).

## Reference
- `internal/api/ledger.go` — style + auth pattern to mirror
- Plan: `OX_KB_DISABLE=1` skips the `/api/v1/kb` source entirely (legacy-only escape hatch)

2. **Session truncated at plan mode exit**: Recording ends at seq=32 "[Request interrupted by user for tool use]" which corresponds to ExitPlanMode. The entire implementation phase is missing: parallel subagent execution (3 agents), code changes to 4 files, build/lint/test verification, beads issue management, git commit, git push, and PR creation. This is ~80% of the session value.

3. **Plan content not captured**: The plan was written to a file via the Write tool but the plan content itself doesn't appear in raw.jsonl (tool entries show [0 chars]). Similarly, all subagent results are absent.

## Expected Behavior

- raw.jsonl should NOT include any entries from before ox agent session start completes
- raw.jsonl should include ALL entries from session start up to (but not including) ox agent session stop  
- Tool results (especially Write, Task subagent results) should have their content captured, not [0 chars]

## Observed Behavior

- 33 entries in raw.jsonl, 3 of which predate session start
- Recording stops at ExitPlanMode (seq=32), missing the entire implementation
- Most tool results show [0 chars] content

Ledger path: ledger/sessions/2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO/
Local cache: Library/Caches/sageox/sessions/repo_019c5812.../sessions/2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO/

title: Consolidate SessionMeta construction into shared builder

1. cmd/ox/agent_session.go:829 — main session stop (richest: Model, Title, Summary)
2. cmd/ox/agent_session_recover.go:174 — recovery (subset: no Model, Title, Summary)
3. cmd/ox/session_upload_cmd.go:128 — manual upload (has its own buildSessionMeta helper)
4. cmd/ox/doctor_session_upload_retry.go:261 — doctor retry (copies from orphan.Meta)

## Proposed Approach
Add a builder/constructor to internal/lfs/meta.go that all sites use. Options:
- Functional options pattern: lfs.NewSessionMeta(name, opts...)
- Builder with required + optional fields
- Simple constructor with commonly-shared fields + setters for optional ones

The key insight: sites 1 and 2 both have agent state, site 4 copies from existing meta, site 3 reconstructs from dir name. A constructor with required fields (Version, SessionName, Username, AgentID, AgentType, CreatedAt, Files) plus chainable setters for optional fields (Model, Title, Summary, EntryCount) would cover all cases cleanly.

title: fix: daemon persistLedgerPath writes empty path due to stale config cache
description:
## Symptom

`ox daemon status` shows ledger as 'synced' but `ox status` shows 'not cloned' for the same ledger path.

Observed on ~/Documents/Code/sageox/sageox-init where config.local.toml had:
```toml
[ledger]
path = ''
last_sync = 2026-02-18T06:10:41.576431Z
```

The daemon was syncing correctly (updating last_sync), but the path was empty — causing ox status to report 'not cloned'.

## Root Cause

Race condition between `persistLedgerPath()` and `UpdateConfigLastSync()` in the daemon. They use different config objects:

1. `persistLedgerPath()` loads a **fresh** config from disk via `config.LoadLocalConfig()`, writes `Path = '/correct/path'`, and saves to disk.
2. `UpdateConfigLastSync()` uses the workspace registry's in-memory `localConfigCache`, which still has `Ledger.Path == ''`.
3. When `UpdateConfigLastSync()` saves the stale cache to disk, it **overwrites** the path that `persistLedgerPath()` just wrote.

The sequence:
- Daemon starts, `localConfigCache` loaded with `Ledger == nil`
- `UpdateConfigLastSync('ledger')` creates `LedgerConfig{}` with empty Path in cache, saves to disk → `path = ''` in TOML
- `persistLedgerPath()` loads fresh config from disk, sees `Path == ''`, writes correct path to disk
- Next sync: `UpdateConfigLastSync('ledger')` saves cache (still has `Path == ''`) → overwrites the correct path

## Code Paths

**Daemon (works):** `WorkspaceRegistry.rebuildFromConfigLocked()` skips empty path, falls through to `InitializeLedger()` which computes the default path via `config.DefaultLedgerPath()`. Daemon knows the real path.

**ox status (broken):** `cmd/ox/status.go:1409` checks `localCfg.Ledger == nil` but NOT `localCfg.Ledger.Path == ''`. When the struct exists with empty path, the fallback to `ledger.DefaultPath()` never fires, and the `hasLedger` check at line 535 (`Path \!= ''`) is false → shows 'not cloned'.

## Suggested Fixes

### Fix 1: Root cause — persistLedgerPath should use the registry cache
Add `PersistLedgerPath(path)` method to `WorkspaceRegistry` that updates the `localConfigCache` directly, keeping it in sync with `UpdateConfigLastSync()`. Change `persistLedgerPath()` to call this instead of loading a separate config copy.

### Fix 2: Defensive — ox status should handle empty path
Change `cmd/ox/status.go:1409` from `localCfg.Ledger == nil` to `localCfg.Ledger == nil || localCfg.Ledger.Path == ''` so it falls back to default path discovery.

### Fix 3: Remove unused import
After fix 1, `internal/daemon/sync.go` no longer needs the `config` package import.

## Files Changed

- `internal/daemon/workspace_registry.go` — add `PersistLedgerPath()` method
- `internal/daemon/sync.go` — simplify `persistLedgerPath()`, remove unused config import
- `cmd/ox/status.go` — defensive empty-path fallback

title: Decide push semantics: pushMurmurCommits is the only daemon write today — kb policy?
description:
## Why
Discovered while reading `internal/daemon/sync.go::pushMurmurCommits` (lines 1306-1340): the daemon DOES push to the ledger remote, contradicting the literal reading of `.claude/rules/daemon-git.md` ('Daemon reads (pull), CLI writes'). This is an authorized exception specifically for murmurs (natural batching every 60s on the ledger sync cycle, with `gitutil.PushWithRetry` and auto-resolve prefixes from `ledger.AutoResolvePrefixes`).

After unification, the question is: which kb types inherit this push behavior? The naive answer is "only type=repo" — but `personal` and `profile` bubbles also accept murmurs (per the kb plan). If they don't push, murmurs accumulate locally forever.

## Decision required
Pick exactly one:
1. **type=repo only** pushes from the daemon. personal/profile murmurs are pushed by CLI only (e.g., on `ox murmur` invocation). Aligns with daemon-git.md spirit; needs CLI-side push wiring for personal/profile.
2. **All writable types** (repo, personal, profile, possibly team) push from the daemon on the kb sync cycle. Needs `push_policy` directive in the manifest (see ox-yvc1.11) and per-type credential/auth handling.
3. **No daemon-side push at all** — delete `pushMurmurCommits` and route all murmur pushes through CLI / IPC. Simplest, but changes when murmurs reach teammates (potentially multi-minute delay).

## Read first
- `internal/daemon/sync.go::pushMurmurCommits` (1306-1340)
- `internal/gitutil/push.go::PushWithRetry`
- `internal/ledger/ledger.go::AutoResolvePrefixes`
- `cmd/ox/murmur.go` for the CLI-side path
- `.claude/rules/daemon-git.md` (the rule this exception breaks)

## Acceptance
- Decision recorded in the type-spec doc (ox-yvc1.2).
- If options 1 or 2: identify which bead implements the per-type push wiring (likely a follow-up).
- If option 3: identify the CLI murmur-push path and confirm it can guarantee timely delivery without the daemon's natural batching.

## Risks
- This is a user-visible latency tradeoff. Murmurs are how teammates see WIP; long delays defeat the purpose.
- The current `s.ledgerMu` mutex coordinates pull-vs-push for the ledger. If multiple kb types push, mutex strategy needs revisiting (per-bubble mutex? per-type? single daemon-wide?).

title: Unify GC: collapse blue-green (sync_gc.go) and kb soft-trash (sync_gc_kb.go)
description:
## Why
Two parallel GC paths today:
- `sync_gc.go::checkAndRunGC` → blue-green reclone for ledger + team contexts (in-place via `runBlueGreenGC`, reopens whisper store after ledger swap).
- `sync_gc_kb.go::runKBGC` → triage-then-reap with `.trash/<kb_id>-<ts>` and 7-day grace.

These have different safety properties: blue-green never deletes data because it preserves dirty files; kb-GC never deletes pre-grace because of `.trash`. The unification needs ONE path where the safety property is explicit per type, not implicit per code path.

## Specific behavior to migrate
Define a `GCPolicy` per kb type:
- `repo`/`team` (today: blue-green) — preserves dirty files, immediate disk reclaim, requires whisper-store reopen for ledger.
- `personal`/`profile`/`custom`/`unknown` (today: kb soft-trash) — 7-day grace, no dirty preservation needed (read-only typical).

Or pick ONE policy and apply universally. Recommend: extend kb soft-trash to all types, BUT add a "reclone immediately on staleness" trigger that mirrors blue-green's interval/full-clone-upgrade triggers. Decision belongs to ox-yvc1.2 type-spec; this bead implements whichever the spec picks.

## Read first
- `internal/daemon/sync_gc.go` (~330 lines; especially `checkAndRunGC`, `runBlueGreenGC`, `reopenWhisperStoreAfterGC`)
- `internal/daemon/sync_gc_kb.go` (~250 lines; especially `runKBGC`, `kbGCTriage`, `kbGCReap`)

- `manifest.DefaultGCIntervalDays` (today applied to ledger + team only)
- The single `gcInProgress` atomic flag at top of `checkAndRunGC` — must remain to prevent overlap.

## Files to change
- New `internal/daemon/sync_gc_unified.go` (or rename `sync_gc.go`) with one entry point: `checkAndRunGC(ctx)` that iterates all kb types via `GCPolicy`.
- Delete `runKBGC` if soft-trash becomes universal, OR keep both helpers behind a per-type policy switch.
- Preserve `reopenWhisperStoreAfterGC` for type=repo (and document why it's not needed for type=team — team-context whisper stores are at `paths.TeamWhisperDBDir`, NOT inside the cloned dir).

## Tests
- Merge `sync_gc_bluegreen_test.go` + `sync_gc_kb_basic_test.go` into a single table-driven harness over kb type.
- Confirm `IssueTypeDirtyWorkspace` is still raised for type=repo when blue-green can't preserve dirty files.
- New: regression for the .trash 7-day grace boundary at every kb type that uses it.

## Risks
- The `cloneInFlight` map is keyed by workspace ID (sync_gc.go:56). KB code uses kb_id. Unify the key (recommend kb_id since it's stable across types).
- `gcInProgress` is a single binary flag; with all types running in one pass, a slow type=repo reclone blocks type=team triage. Consider per-type sub-locks.

title: runKBGC must consult cloneInFlight to avoid triaging mid-clone
description:
Discovered while implementing ox-gzp.18 kb GC bluegreen test parity.

## Problem
`internal/daemon/sync_gc_kb.go::runKBGC` does not consult `s.cloneInFlight` before triaging a kb dir. The kb sync loop's `cloneBubble` may have created the parent dir via `os.MkdirAll` and then begun a `git clone` into it. If the GC tick fires during the clone window AND the API list lags such that the kb_id is briefly absent from `listFn`'s response, the partial directory will be `os.Rename`d into `.trash/`. The active `git clone` subprocess will then be writing into a renamed inode, producing a half-cloned bubble that "looks fine" until the next pull.

## Repro shape (race window)
1. `cloneBubble` runs `os.MkdirAll(parent, ...)` + spawns `git clone target`.
2. Concurrent GC tick fires; `kbAPIListFn` returns a list missing kb_id (transient API hiccup or stale read).
3. Triage renames `target/` → `.trash/<kb_id>-<ts>/`.
4. The clone subprocess finishes writing to the renamed path.
5. Next sync pass: canonical path missing, kb_id back in API → fresh clone starts. The just-finished clone in trash is dead.

## Fix sketch
In `kbGCTriage`, after the `if _, ok := want[name]; ok { continue }` line, add:
```go
if _, inflight := s.cloneInFlight.Load(name); inflight {
    continue // active clone — never triage
}
```
The `cloneBubble` flow uses kb_id as the workspaceID for `cloneInFlight` (verify via `internal/daemon/sync_clone.go`), so the lookup is by name without translation.

## Test
Existing test `TestKBGC_RespectsCloneInFlight_DoesNotTriageActiveClone` in `internal/daemon/sync_gc_kb_bluegreen_test.go` is currently `t.Skip("FUTURE: ...")`. When this fix lands, remove the skip — the test asserts the desired post-fix behavior.

## References
- `internal/daemon/sync_gc_kb.go` (runKBGC, kbGCTriage)
- `internal/daemon/sync_clone.go` (cloneInFlight pattern)
- `internal/daemon/sync_gc_bluegreen_test.go` (parallel pattern in team_gc world: `TestBlueGreenGC_SkipsCloneInFlight`)

## Severity
Race window is narrow in practice (the same API list call typically feeds both sync and GC), but the failure mode is silent data corruption inside the cloned bubble. Production impact: a user on a flaky network could see one bubble fail to clone correctly, with no error surfaced until the next pull diverges.

title: Consolidate three diverged HTML generation paths into single pipeline
description:
Three separate HTML rendering pipelines have diverged, causing repeated bugs where fixes to one path don't apply to others (see ox-aql).

**Current state — three paths:**

| Path | File | Used by | Template |
|------|------|---------|----------|
| 1 | internal/session/html/ | ox session stop, ox agent <id> session stop | Embedded assets |
| 2 | cmd/ox/session_html.go | ox session export, ox session push-summary | Inline const strings |
| 3 | cmd/ox/session_view_html.go | ox session view --html | Inline const strings |

**Duplicated logic (copy-pasted, then diverged):**
- Entry type mapping (mapEntryType vs viewHTMLMapEntryType vs normalizeMessageType)
- Role-to-type mapping
- HTML escaping, output truncation
- Title generation
- Timestamp parsing (ts vs timestamp, RFC3339 vs RFC3339Nano)
- Root-level vs nested content extraction
- CSS/JS (inline strings in paths 2+3, embedded assets in path 1)

**Missing from some paths:**
- Path 1: no diff rendering, no collapsible tool messages
- Path 3: no sender labels, no summary/aha moments, no keyboard shortcuts
- Path 2: uses local openInBrowser() instead of cli.OpenInBrowser (canonical violation)
- Path 3: dead code (processContentWithMermaid — defined, never called)

**Proposed approach:**
Converge on a single rendering pipeline in internal/session/html/ that all command paths feed into, with options struct for toggling features (summary panel, sender labels, aha moments, etc.). Entry type mapping, timestamp parsing, content extraction, and CSS/JS live in one place.

## Test Coverage Audit

**Path 3 (session_view_html.go) has ZERO tests** — this is the path where all three rendering bugs in ox-aql were found. No tests for viewHTMLBuildMessageView, viewHTMLMapEntryType, viewHTMLMapRoleToType, or any of the viewHTML* functions.

**Markdown generator (internal/session/markdown.go) has ZERO tests** — the MarkdownGenerator used by session stop/export has no JSONL-in → markdown-out tests at all.

### What needs testing (minimum):

1. **viewHTMLMapEntryType** — table-driven test covering user, assistant, message, tool_call, tool_result, tool, system, unknown (this is where the bug was)
2. **viewHTMLBuildMessageView** — test with:
   - Root-level content (imported JSONL format)
   - Nested data.content (standard format)
   - ts field (imported) vs timestamp field (standard)
   - user/assistant/tool entry types at root level
3. **viewHTMLBuildTemplateData** — end-to-end: _meta header + entries → template data with correct metadata, message count, types
4. **MarkdownGenerator.Generate** — JSONL session → markdown output, verify entries appear with correct formatting
5. **Cross-format integration tests** — same JSONL input through all three HTML paths should produce equivalent content (different styling is fine, missing entries is not)

### Consolidation reduces test burden:
Once paths converge into single pipeline (the main fix), these duplicated test concerns collapse into one test suite.

title: (Maybe) ox kb migrate: relocate legacy ledger + team-context dirs to kb_id-keyed layout
description:
## Why
Today the ledger lives at `~/.local/share/sageox/<endpoint>/ledgers/<repo_id>/` and team contexts at `~/.local/share/sageox/<endpoint>/teams/<team_id>/`. KB bubbles live at `~/.local/share/sageox/<endpoint>/kb/<kb_id>/`. After unification, the canonical layout is the kb_id-keyed `kb/` tree for every bubble type. Existing on-disk dirs need to either (a) be migrated by an explicit `ox kb migrate` command, or (b) be transparently aliased via the symlink reconciler so users never see the change.

## Decision required (this bead's first deliverable)
Confirm one of:
- **Option A:** No migration tool needed. The daemon's `reconcileAllProjectSymlinks` (already in `sync_bubbles.go`) plus per-bubble symlinks make the legacy paths irrelevant. Doctor flags any orphans.
- **Option B:** A migration tool is needed. Implement `ox kb migrate` that walks legacy dirs, asks the API for the kb_id mapping, and `os.Rename`s into the kb tree.

Recommend Option A unless the inventory (ox-yvc1.1) reveals a path resolution that breaks (e.g., codedb indexes that reference the absolute ledger path and don't survive a rename).

## Read first
- `internal/paths/paths.go::KBDir`, `TeamContextDir`, ledger path resolver in `internal/config/local_config.go::DefaultLedgerPath`
- `internal/daemon/sync_bubbles_symlinks.go` (or equivalent — symlink reconciler)
- `cmd/ox/doctor_*.go` for legacy-detection checks

## If Option B chosen
- New file `cmd/ox/kb_migrate.go` mirroring the shape of `cmd/ox/kb_hydrate.go` (already on this branch).
- Idempotent: re-running on a migrated tree is a no-op.
- Dry-run mode default; `--apply` to actually move.
- Fix codedb path references after move (this is the non-trivial piece).

## Tests
- For Option A: a doctor test asserting legacy dirs surface as a fixable warning.
- For Option B: a CLI test running migrate on a synthetic legacy tree and asserting post-state.

## Risks
- codedb's bleve index stores absolute paths. A rename without rebuilding the index leaves a stale reference. Confirm before choosing Option A.
- Symlink-only migration on Windows is fragile (junction points behave differently). Even if Option A is chosen for POSIX, a real migration tool may be needed for Windows.

title: Delete ledger doPull and team-context doTeamSync after one-release shim window

## Why
After ox-yvc1.5 and ox-yvc1.6 land, `internal/daemon/sync.go::doPull` (and the smaller `pullChanges`, `pullTeamContexts`, `doTeamSync` shims) are dead weight kept alive for one release for back-compat. This bead exists to make the deletion intentional, not accidental — gated on:

1. A CHANGELOG entry naming the cutover release.
2. Telemetry showing zero callers using the old shim paths for at least one release.
3. The twin consolidation (ox-yvc1.10) is done — otherwise tests still reach into the deleted paths.

## Specific behavior
- Delete `pullChanges`, `doPull`, `pullTeamContexts`, `doTeamSync`, `pullTeamContext` (singular) once shimmed callers are gone.
- Delete `internal/daemon/sync_team.go` entirely if no team-only logic remains.
- Keep the small entry points (`SyncWithProgress`, `TeamSync`) since they are IPC surfaces — back them with kb directly.

## Read first
- The migrated state of `internal/daemon/sync.go` and `internal/daemon/sync_team.go` after ox-yvc1.5/6 land.
- `internal/daemon/sync.go::Start` ticker registration (must collapse the dual-tick to a single kb tick driven by the cadence registry from ox-yvc1.3).
- IPC handlers in `daemon.go` (~line 1587: `BackgroundStarted`, `Sync`, `TeamSync` etc.) — confirm none reach into deleted helpers.

## Files to change
- `internal/daemon/sync.go`: delete the dead shim functions.
- `internal/daemon/sync_team.go`: delete the file (or shrink to a one-liner re-export of `TeamContextStatus` if still used).
- Any test files that import the deleted symbols: migrate or delete.

## Tests
- The full test suite must still pass.
- The diff should be net-negative LoC (~500+ lines removed). Any net-positive diff means the migration absorbed responsibilities it shouldn't have.

## Risks
- External integrations (e.g., the cloud API client lib) may import daemon types. Confirm no public surface breaks.
- Telemetry attribution: today metrics `RecordTeamSync`/`RecordTeamSyncError` are typed by source. Replace with kb-typed metrics BEFORE deletion or dashboards break.

title: Spec: kb-superset additions to sync.manifest schema (lfs_hydrate_policy, cadence_override, gc_policy)
description:
## Why
Once kb is canonical, the per-bubble `sync.manifest` should grow optional fields that today don't exist in the team-context-flavored manifest. We don't need to ship the implementation in one bead — we need a written schema so future PRs reference one source of truth instead of inventing field names ad-hoc.

## Deliverable
`docs/ai/specs/manifest-v2.md` (or extend the existing manifest doc) covering proposed new directives:

- `lfs_hydrate_policy` ∈ {`eager`, `on-demand`, `never`} — controls `internal/lfs/hydrate.go` invocation. Today hydration is opt-in via CLI; this directive lets the bubble's owner declare expected behavior.
- `cadence_override` (duration string, min 30s) — overrides the type-default cadence. Useful when a single team's bubble updates rarely and 15s is wasteful.
- `gc_policy` ∈ {`blue-green`, `soft-trash`} — explicit choice instead of implicit-by-type. Enables a `personal` bubble to opt into blue-green if it cares about disk reclaim.
- `push_policy` ∈ {`none`, `murmurs-only`, `cli-driven`} — declares whether the daemon may push (today only ledger via `pushMurmurCommits`).
- `min_grace_period_days` — trash grace override for soft-trash bubbles.

## Read first
- `internal/manifest/parser.go` (current directives + `SupportedVersion`)
- `internal/manifest/types.go` (struct shape)
- `internal/lfs/hydrate.go` (new in branch — see `cmd/ox/kb_hydrate.go`, `internal/lfs/hydrate.go`)
- The type-spec from ox-yvc1.2

## Acceptance
- Spec doc lists each new directive with: type signature, default, example, validation rules, version-bump implications.
- Each directive's IMPLEMENTATION lives in a follow-up bead (this bead is decision-only). File those follow-ups against the parent epic if scoped, or note them as future work.
- `SupportedVersion` bump strategy decided: bump to 2 if any breaking change; keep at 1 if all additions are optional.

## Risks
- Manifest is the contract between server-seeded bubbles and the daemon. Field additions must be backward-compatible (parser already warns on unknown directives — that's the safety net).

title: Unify status surface: collapse per-type sections in cmd/ox/status.go into kb summary
